svg.title: The four scalability limits of VPLS and the mitigation for each
svg.desc: Four cards in two columns. MAC learning, where every PE must hold every customer MAC so memory becomes the constraint. Full mesh pseudowires, whose count grows as the square of the PE count. Flooding of unknown unicast, broadcast and ARP, which consumes bandwidth at every site. And the absence of a control plane, where MACs are learned only in the data plane, so convergence is slow. Each card lists its mitigations, with EVPN or PBB appearing in three of the four. A red note at the bottom says the real problem is not performance but the missing control plane: learning by flooding, multihoming by MC-LAG and recovery by re-flooding are all patches applied in the data plane.
svg.text: Four limits, and only one of them is about bandwidth
Read the mitigations column: three of the four point at the same answer, and it is not a faster link
MAC learning
Every PE must hold every customer MAC in the domain.
At scale it is memory and table churn, not CPU.
MITIGATION
cap MACs per VPLS · tune aging · PBB (MAC-in-MAC)
symptom: silent drops of new MACs once the table is full
Full-mesh pseudowires
The pseudowire count grows as O(n²), and every PE
carries the configuration for every other PE.
MITIGATION
H-VPLS hierarchy · EVPN
symptom: adding a site becomes a change window
Flooding
Unknown unicast, broadcast and ARP are flooded to
every site. One site’s ARP storm is everyone’s.
MITIGATION
ARP proxy · multicast optimisation · EVPN
symptom: the complaint is "the network is slow" with no fault
No control plane
MACs exist only in the data plane, so a failure is
resolved by ageing, re-flooding and re-learning.
MITIGATION
EVPN: advertise MACs in BGP
symptom: convergence measured in tens of seconds

text.tspan: The CCDE judgement: VPLS’s problem is not performance, it is the absence of a control plane.

svg.text: Learning by flooding, multihoming by MC-LAG, recovery by re-flooding — three different symptoms, one root cause, and all three are patches applied in the data plane.
EVPN exists to move that machinery into the control plane, which is why it keeps returning in later chapters.
